Device busy is interval union of actual kernels/copies/memsets across streams. API inclusive time, kernel sum and wall are not additive. EventSynchronize often overlaps actual GPU execution and is not removable overhead.

Each token envelope runs from previous4B DtoH hostAPI end to current4B DtoH hostAPI end. Snapshot publication is after token read and can be shifted into the next envelope; final publication is outside the last endpoint. These envelopes are not exact source phase/step clocks.

No traced device activity is a measurable union complement. An interval with no recorded API is not a CPU-function measurement, proof of CPU idleness or proof it is removable; CPU sampling is disabled.
Copy payload GPU durations/bytes are reported separately from memcpy submission API durations and GraphLaunch costs; overlapping time cannot be summed into a claimed total saving.

conclusions: Actual extra payload-copy device time is about23us/decode, not evidence that copy bandwidth alone explains the unprofiled loss.
Seven graph submissions versus one and23.25eagerD2D copies/decode are real extra mechanisms. Six inter-capture transitions contain observed device gaps; they are not guaranteed recoverable time.
Recurring event construction is absent in90pure-reuse calls in both arms; do not optimize an imagined per-append EventCreate hotspot.
Unmarked no-device/no-API gaps grow with history in paged and remain lower in dense. CPU sampling was disabled, so no individual C++ function share is proven.
Instrumented total envelope reverses unprofiled ordering; counts and bounded gap mechanisms inform next implementation, not a tokens/s win or attribution of the full3% loss.
